requirements.text: The new consolidated group should named 'Unified Reliability Squad', categorised as 'IT Support' ... assign any active manager to oversee this newly created group
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_group WHERE group_id = 'GROUP_005' AND name = 'Unified Reliability Squad' AND type = 'IT Support' AND manager_id IN ('USER_002', 'USER_008') AND active = 1
requirements.source: New unified group created with correct properties
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (GROUP_005 after GROUP_004); the task creates exactly one group, the benchmark's group check selects by name only and its membership check already uses GROUP_005
'categorised as' maps to the type column, the only category-like column of user_group

'any active manager': the seed's active users with role manager are USER_002 (Priya Sharma, ORG_001) and USER_008 (Sophie Mueller, ORG_002), so either is accepted as the benchmark check does; the request does not restrict the choice by organisation
active = 1 kept from the benchmark check; a group created 'to work together' is read as active, the request does not state it
org_id, email and description not fixed by request or policy; not tested

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_group WHERE group_id IN ('GROUP_003', 'GROUP_004') AND active = 0

assumptions: 'IT Support Team' resolves to GROUP_003 and 'Infrastructure Team' to GROUP_004 (both ORG_002, same site, manager USER_008, both active on the seed)
'dissolving' is read as deactivating (active = 0): it is the only column that retires a group, update_user_group is the only tool that writes user_group, and no tool deletes a group
the request does not say to remove the old memberships and no tool removes one; not tested

requirements.text: Add everyone who belongs to the those team groups

requirements.source: All members from the old groups are now members of the new unified group
assumptions: USER_009 (Kenji Tanaka) is the only member of GROUP_003 on the seed
two memberships are created and the request fixes no order, so each is selected by its natural key (group, user), not by member_id; the new group's id is assumed GROUP_005, next in sequence

notes: Merged from two passes that agree on all three benchmark checks (kept), the new group (GROUP_005: Unified Reliability Squad, IT Support, manager USER_002 or USER_008, active), the deactivation of GROUP_003 and GROUP_004, the two new memberships (USER_009, USER_008) and the two boundary stays (the other groups' members stay out of GROUP_005; GROUP_001 and GROUP_002 stay active). disagreement: the membership check's structure: A carries it as one requirement with a count of 2 over user_id IN ('USER_009', 'USER_008'), B as one natural-key requirement per member; kept B's split as the tighter form and because several rows created in one table in no fixed order are each selected by their natural key, with the benchmark check carried jointly by both (logged in each). disagreement: cells of the two memberships and the two stays: A leaves cells empty, B repeats the selector's columns; chose the row key (user ids or group ids) in the selector and the tested column (group_id = GROUP_005, active = 1) as the cell, so each selector names the rows and cells carries the tested column without repeating it; no sql changed (logged in each). The acting user Marcus Thompson (USER_001) is an admin; the policy says nothing about groups, so no policy defaults were applied. The two old teams and their members are all ORG_002 and USER_008 (their manager) is the only ORG_002 manager, but the request says 'any active manager' and does not restrict the choice by organisation, so both are accepted as the benchmark does. No remove requirement: the request asks for the old teams to be dissolved (deactivated, as the benchmark tests) and for their members to be added to the new group, not for the old membership rows (MEMBER_004, MEMBER_005) to be deleted, and no listed tool removes a membership; both passes agree. revised: the membership requirements' assumptions and these notes now state the reasons for the natural-key selectors and the cell layout directly, instead of pointing to a rule or to other files.
